I will keep this year simple and steady. I am 58, I have farmed for 40 years, and my family has some off-farm work, so I do not want a plan that is too scattered or too labor-heavy. I will put most of my land into the wheat-maize rotation because I know it well, it fits my irrigated conditions, and it gives me stable grain and feed income. I will keep a smaller block in stevia because it can bring cash, but it needs more careful field management, so I will not expand it too much. On the wheat-maize land, I will use better seed, put fertilizer in a moderate but reliable way, irrigate on time with my well, and keep pesticide sprays limited to what I think is necessary. For maize, I will use hybrid seed and keep costs under control with no-tillage after wheat harvest. For stevia, I will manage it more carefully with a little more potassium and more irrigation because I want stable leaf yield and quality.
